mathematical_proof.method: Independent exact fold-orbit enumeration, source JPG and formal PNG viewed at native scale
mathematical_proof.coordinate_setup: Original square [-1,1]^2; perpendicular half folds leave Q=[0,1]^2, up to orientation. Every removal unfolds by (u,v)->(s*u,t*v) for s,t in {-1,+1}. A straight corner clip meets both adjacent sides at positive distances a,b. Its cut segment has two nonzero components.

exhaustive_four_cases.unfolded_removal: Four separate right triangles at all four original outer corners
exhaustive_four_cases.construction: Remove (1-u)/a+(1-v)/b<1 near (1,1), with 0<a,b<1; reflect across both axes. The outer boundary is an octagon.

exhaustive_four_cases.unfolded_removal: Two V notches at opposite top and bottom side midpoints
exhaustive_four_cases.construction: Remove u/a+(1-v)/b<1 near (0,1); reflection in u=0 joins two half triangles into one V notch; reflection in v=0 creates its opposite.

exhaustive_four_cases.unfolded_removal: Two V notches at opposite left and right side midpoints
exhaustive_four_cases.construction: Remove (1-u)/a+v/b<1 near (1,0); reflect in v=0, then u=0.

exhaustive_four_cases.unfolded_removal: One central diamond or axis-diagonal rhombus hole
exhaustive_four_cases.construction: Remove u/a+v/b<1 near (0,0); unfolded hole |x|/a+|y|/b<1. For a=b its vertices are (+/-a,0),(0,+/-a).

mathematical_proof.exclusion_of_E: Only the centre-centre corner can make a bounded internal hole. That hole has four oblique sides with directions (+/-a,+/-b); no side is parallel to an original sheet edge when a,b>0. E has four axis-parallel inner sides, so is not that hole. The other three cases meet the outer boundary, and cannot make E either. All A/B/C/D have explicit constructions above. Thus E is uniquely impossible.
mathematical_proof.freedom_preserved: The final displayed clipped corner is an illustrative possible corner, not an additional restriction to one fold-corner type. All four corners were enumerated; no annotation may choose one as a new given.

reference_and_history.reference: Current Solid167 C01 distinguishes two real source features red/blue and corresponding two candidate groups. The current A option, all nine current PNGs and their actual plugins were inspected.
reference_and_history.transfer: This question has one freely placed corner cut, so inventing a second cut or fixing a corner is prohibited. The two actual orthogonal fold-axis guides instead supply source directions, mapped to E aperture sides.
reference_and_history.old_history: No tested old candidate exists for Plane194. Old prescreen correctly rejected simply coloring a real cut and C diamond as a route to declaring C impossible: that would need unsupported polarity inversion.
reference_and_history.material_difference_from_old_prescreen: This design does not pair the real cut with C. It pairs fold-axis directions with the geometrically wrong E square aperture. The prospective mistake accepts E as the central-corner result and rejects its competing central aperture C. A/B/D outer-boundary cases remain distinct. Thus the proposed C error is a cut-edge-versus-fold-axis confusion, not merely reading cannot as can.
reference_and_history.no_new_given: Neither fold guide selects which quarter-sheet corner is cut. The source actual cut and discarded-corner ghost legs remain black.
reference_and_history.semantic_check: The colored dashed source guides already denote future fold axes: each is shown only in its own construction stage and omitted in the subsequent quarter-square. They are conventional operation guides, not transported paper surface edging. No source material outline is colored. All physically possible samples A/B/C/D are completely unchanged. Coloring E cannot make its square aperture realizable under either external-annotation or colored-edging reading. E stays the unique impossible sample.
reference_and_history.limitations: Prediction is prospective and fallible; no model response has yet been seen for these pixels. Same logical family as Plane245 is applied to a different formal question and its own independently checked source.

literal_color_reading: No moving source paper boundary is colored. The only colored option E is impossible already by geometry; A/B/C/D remain unmarked and have the explicit constructions in the four-case proof. Colors on conventional dashed folding guides do not prescribe any new cut or printed pattern.
